summary: The strongest result is an IP-Glasma calculation that unifies soft and semi-hard production to quantify centrality bias across p+O, p+Pb, O+O, and Pb+Pb, while leaving a suppression deficit consistent with final-state energy loss. Other notable work addresses non-Gaussian femtoscopic sources, self-supervised detector calibration, calibrated nuclear optical-potential uncertainties, unbinned neural inference, and cross-geometry calorimeter simulation.
professional_summary: Initial-state hard-soft correlations and centrality-dependent nuclear modification; non-Gaussian femtoscopic source structure; self-supervised detector calibration; differentiable uncertainty quantification; hybrid neural density estimation; cross-geometry calorimeter fast simulation.
strongest_paper: 2609.29886: initial-state nuclear modification and hard-soft correlations in IP-Glasma
strongest_paper_summary: IP-Glasma provides a multi-system initial-state baseline for R_AB and exposes the additional suppression that final-state energy loss must explain.

papers.title: Centrality-dependent nuclear modification from hard-soft correlations in the glasma
papers.summary: IP-Glasma predicts centrality-dependent R_AB across p+O, p+Pb, O+O, and Pb+Pb from initial-state physics and leaves additional O+O and Pb+Pb suppression for final-state energy loss to explain.
papers.abstract: First predictions from IP-Glasma for centrality-dependent nuclear modification using a common description of soft and semi-hard production, with HERA-calibrated proton structure and event-by-event color-field fluctuations.

papers.title: Simulating the emission source function in very peripheral relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: A hybrid transport calculation decomposes peripheral Pb-Pb emission sources and finds that a Gaussian-plus-exponential form captures their compact core and long tail better than a Gaussian.
papers.abstract: A microscopic femtoscopic analysis reconstructs source functions for meson, baryon, and cross-species pairs and separates primordial, rescattering, and resonance-decay contributions.

papers.title: Measuring short-range correlations using relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: Large-to-small-radius spectator-neutron yield ratios are proposed as probes of the SRC-induced high-momentum tail and its isospin dependence.
papers.abstract: The proposal uses the transverse displacement of spectator neutrons in relativistic ion collisions, including a Zr-96/Ru-96 ratio, to access short-range nuclear correlations.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning for Joint Wire Calibration and Interaction Position Reconstruction in Multi-Wire Parallel Plate Avalanche Counters
papers.summary: A self-supervised differentiable calibration tested on real VAMOS++ data improves independently measured position resolution by 33% and 44% over the conventional method.
papers.abstract: Global wire gains and event-level positions are inferred jointly from geometry and charge-energy constraints without labelled positions or dedicated calibration runs.

papers.title: Rapid Uncertainty Quantification on a Latent Field using Fisher Information
papers.summary: Sampling-free local-Gaussian UQ reaches 96.0% coverage for nominal 95% held-out intervals that are 30% narrower than KDUQ, but coverage falls to 89.3% out of distribution.
papers.abstract: Fisher information and a differentiable scattering solver propagate uncertainty from an inferred nuclear optical-potential field to observables.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Inference and Unbinned Asimov Construction with Hybrid Neural Density Estimation
papers.summary: The hybrid density construction is technically careful and supports exact finite-sample closure for the learned likelihood, but it is validated only on a controlled analytic HEP-like toy.
papers.abstract: A parameter-independent flow reference combined with classifier density ratios yields evaluable densities, renewable pseudo-experiments, importance sampling, and unbinned Asimov datasets.

papers.title: Cross-geometry transfer and model collapse in point cloud calorimeter shower generation
papers.summary: With 100 target showers, transfer improves geometric-mean Wasserstein distance by about 51% over scratch training; evidence is limited to one source-target pair and a proceedings-length study.
papers.abstract: CaloClouds II transfers between detector geometries, supports parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and shows progressive model collapse under recursive synthetic retraining.

cautions.title: Quarkonium production in light-ion collisions with the ALICE experiment
cautions.summary: Potentially important new-system quarkonium data, but the four-page proceedings abstract contains no numerical result, uncertainty, or model-discriminating conclusion.
cautions.abstract: The contribution motivates forward-rapidity charmonium measurements in 2025 O-O and p-O data and states that new measurements will be shown and compared with models.
